# Generated by Manarouter for issue #10. Deploy it with:
#     cerebrium deploy -y --detach
#
# Every key written here is written because the platform default is wrong for a vLLM server: a
# deploy replaces the whole app record, so an omitted key is reset to its default rather than
# preserved. Keys left out are left out on purpose (see `gpu::cerebrium` in `mr-core`).

[cerebrium.deployment]
name = "manarouter-demo"
# The platform default is true, which would publish an app that runs a 30 GB model to anyone who
# finds the URL. Set false, then put a project API key in front of it.
disable_auth = false
# Default 600 s. A cold start has to pull the checkpoint before vLLM binds its port, and 600 s is
# inside the range that has been seen to time out on a large repository. Range 60-7200.
deployment_initialization_timeout = 1800

[cerebrium.runtime.custom]
port = 8000
# The command the container runs. Everything after /{app_name}/ on the inference host is proxied
# to this port, which is why the base URL below is knowable before the first deploy.
entrypoint = ["vllm", "serve", "orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-FP8", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--served-model-name", "orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-FP8"]

[cerebrium.hardware]
# RAM and cores, not VRAM. vLLM keeps the checkpoint on disk and streams it; the memory figure has
# to cover the loader's own copy of the tensors.
cpu = 8.0
memory = 64.0
compute = "HOPPER_H100"
gpu_count = 1

[cerebrium.scaling]
min_replicas = 0
max_replicas = 1
# Default is 1 on GPU compute. Requests per container, not containers.
replica_concurrency = 32
cooldown = 10
# Doubles as the per-request timeout; it is written out because 900 is a bound, not a preference.
response_grace_period = 900
# interruptible is the base rate; protected is billed at 2x and cannot be relocated mid-request.
compute_tier = "interruptible"

[cerebrium.dependencies]
pip = ["vllm"]
warnings: `HOPPER_H100` bills $0.00094/s, which is $3.3984/hour (derived, ×3600); a single replica left warm for an hour costs that whether or not it answers.

`replica_concurrency` is set to 32 from the platform's own vLLM example, because no --max-num-seqs was chosen. The platform default is 1 on GPU compute, which would let one request occupy a whole card.
`response_grace_period` is set to 900 s, the platform default, because it also bounds a single request: a longer generation is cut off at that point, not at the model's context limit.

`cooldown` is set to 10 s. The platform default is 10 s, so a container is gone before most interactive follow-ups arrive; every request after a cooldown pays a cold start, and no published figure for that exists (see `issue-10-platform-facts.md`).
the vLLM version is unpinned, so the image is whatever `pip install vllm` resolves to on the build. Pin it once a version is known to match the card's CUDA driver.
applies_on_note: this route writes no config, stores no credential and deploys nothing; it renders the file you would otherwise assemble by hand. Run the command from a directory containing this file.
